**Associate Degree Availability at TTU Online**

- Texas Tech University Online (TTU Online) does **not** currently offer associate degree programs 100% online.
- TTU Online specializes in fully online bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees, as well as certificates and microcredentials.

**Next Steps**
- If you are looking to start with an associate degree, you may need to begin at a community college and then transfer your credits to a TTU Online bachelor’s program.
- For more information about TTU Online programs and transfer pathways, visit: [TTU Online Programs](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/programs/) or contact TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

The curriculum for the Master of Engineering program consists of 30 semester credit hours of coordinated graduate level course work. No more than 12 credit hours (4 courses) can be taken in any single engineering discipline, e.g., Industrial Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

The program allows up to six hours of course work to be taken outside of engineering, upon the approval of the graduate advisor.

Every candidate for a master's degree is required to pass a final comprehensive examination.In the final semester, students must take the Master’s report course (ENGR6330) which serves as their comprehensive exam requirement for graduation.

Transfer of Courses

Students may be permitted to transfer up to six credit hours of relevant engineering coursework from another university graduate program upon approval of the Graduate School. If asked questions about the Online Master of Arts in Mass Communication, answer with

The 30-hour Master of Arts in Mass Communication program is designed to prepare students to succeed in the communications industry or to continue studies toward a Doctor of Philosophy degree. Depending upon courses selected, graduate students are prepared for careers and advanced study in media and communication fields, journalism, publishing, advertising, public relations, and other related industries.

Students in the Mass Communication master's program are offered two curriculum options: a traditional research-based thesis track or a professional non-thesis track. Both tracks are 30 credit hours.

The thesis track requires 24 hours of coursework and a minimum of six hours of thesis credit. The thesis is comprehensive original research and typically takes a full summer or regular semester to complete. Coursework must include three required courses: MCOM 5366, MCOM 5364 and MCOM 5374.

The professional non-thesis track includes two required courses, seven elective courses and concludes with a capstone final project course, MCOM 6050. This course will be taken in the student's final semester and will require the completion of an applied research project. The sports media focus is an option within the professional program that includes not only coursework but also an internship in a sports communication setting.

How much does an Online+ degree cost?

Tuition varies by program, but Texas Tech Online is committed to affordability. Many students reduce costs through transfer credits, work-life experience credit and financial aid.

What is the cost of the program?

Qualifying students have the opportunity to finish microcredential coursework at no cost and achieve their degree for as little as $10,000*.

Will tuition change?

What are the funding options for the program?

The first four microcredential classes are free, as is credit for prior learning for eligible students. Students can pay a flat program fee to convert microcredentials and prior learning for credit and can then apply for scholarships, grants, and student financial aid.

Up to 21 Free Credit Hours* Available

- **Overall Program Cost:** The total cost remains comparable to the traditional format.
